cards.explanation: The answer is that it will all be made known. Jesus says, "For there is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known." That's the reason He gives right after telling them not to be afraid of the people against them. Friends, I once hid a burnt batch behind the flour canister. The smell had the whole bakery knowing in about four minutes.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "What I tell you in the dark, speak in the daylight; what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the housetops." So what's whispered in their ears is meant to be spoken out loud. I think that's the biggest volume change I've ever heard of, from a whisper straight to a rooftop.

The answer is soul. Jesus says, "Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul." This is a heavy line, friends, so I'll say it plainly. The ones He's talking about can kill the body, and the soul is the part they cannot kill. I'm glad it's right there in black and white.

The answer is the One who can destroy soul and body. Jesus says, "Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell." It's a serious line, so I'll let it be serious. Notice who He just told them not to fear, the ones who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Now He points them to the One with the real weight.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from the will of your Father." Those are two sparrows sold for a penny, friends. And still the Father's will is in the picture for every one. I think that's the whole point of the comparison.

The answer is more than many sparrows. Jesus says, "So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows." He says it right after the sparrows and the numbered hairs. Friends, not just more than one sparrow, but MORE than many.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "But whoever denies Me before men, I will also deny him before My Father in heaven." It sits right beside the promise about those who confess Him. It's a serious line, friends, so I'll let it stand on its own.

The answer is a sword. Jesus says, "Do not assume that I have come to bring peace to the earth; I have not come to bring peace, but a sword." The next verses show what He means, friends, a man against his father, a daughter against her mother. I'd say that's one to read slowly.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "Anyone who loves his father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me; anyone who loves his son or daughter more than Me is not worthy of Me…" He says it about both directions in a family. I think it's a hard one to hear, and He says it plainly.

The answer is his cross. Jesus says, "…anyone who does not take up his cross and follow Me is not worthy of Me." A follower takes up a cross and follows. Friends, I carry a rolling pin on a normal day. Jesus is talking about something far heavier.

The answer is find. Jesus says, "…whoever loses his life for My sake will find it." It's the other half of the line about finding your life and losing it. The turn is what makes it land. Lose it for His sake and you find it.

The answer is Jesus and the One who sent Him. Jesus says, "He who receives you receives Me, and he who receives Me receives the One who sent Me." That's two steps in one sentence, friends. Receive the disciples and you're receiving Jesus. Receive Jesus and you're receiving the One who sent Him.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "Whoever receives a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward…" Receiving a prophet because he is a prophet comes with a prophet's reward. Friends, I think that's a generous deal. He says the same about receiving a righteous man because he is a righteous man.

The answer is reward. Jesus says, "…truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward." That's for a cup of cold water, friends, given to one of these little ones because he is His disciple. I lose my spatula every week, and Jesus says this reward isn't lost. That's a lot of comfort for something so small.

The answer is that He teaches and preaches in their cities. Matthew 11:1 says, "After Jesus had finished instructing His twelve disciples, He went on from there to teach and preach in their cities." Friends, the instructing is done and Jesus gets right to work. I think the best way to follow a good lesson is to keep going, and He does.
